children: that it intends to acquire World Labs in an $8.2B all-stock deal is being well received on Wall Street.

Citi analyst Atif Malik said the decision to add World Labs and its founder, Fei-Fei Li (widely referred to as the “godmother of AI”), gives the company “deeper visibility” into how AI models are evolving.

“We believe the motivations for this transaction include: 1) acquiring more leading AI engineers (Bloomberg reported today that the company has ~70 employees); 2) better position the company within physical AI, and 3) build better end-to-end systems,” Malik wrote in a note to clients. “We maintain AMD as our favorite growth compute semis pick in 2026.” Malik has a Buy rating and $575 price target on AMD.
AMD shares were up 1.4% in premarket trading on Tuesday.

RBC analyst Srini Pajjuri echoed those sentiments, suggesting that the deal to acquire the privately held AI research lab could "help position the company to offer full-stack solutions for robotics, simulation, and physical AI markets, which are in early stages.”
And while AMD is adding a “world-class team of AI researchers and model experts,” including Lei, to its team, Pajjuri believes Nvidia
still has a “significant” lead in spatial AI and physical simulation with its Omniverse platform. Pajjuri has a Sector Perform rating and a $540 price target on AMD.
Wells Fargo analyst Joe Quatrochi, who has an Overweight rating and $700 price target on AMD, said the deal is all about providing better foresight into the future.

“We think the addition of World Labs further expands AMD's open AI ecosystem—investors are likely to likely look at adjacently to NVDA's ecosystem of Omniverse, Cosmos, and Isaac,” Quatrochi wrote in a note to clients.

title: AMD in focus as Wall Street praises World Labs deal in bid to boost physical AI
